$comment: Design tokens — spacing, layout, radius, elevation. Spec §5.3, §5.4.
Base unit is 4px, not 8px: dense data UI needs sub-8px increments. A table cell
needs 6px vertical padding, and rounding to 8 makes rows 25% taller, costing
visible rows. 4px is the smallest unit that still constrains (§5.3).

layout.$comment: Content caps at 1440px: beyond that, vertical eye-travel between time-aligned panels exceeds comfortable saccade distance and the user stops perceiving them as aligned. The alignment IS the feature (§5.3).

radius.$comment: Charts and data tables use radius 0. A rounded corner on a plot area implies the data is clipped by decoration — the clearest 'web designer touched this' tell (§5.4).

$comment: Elevation is luminance + border, never shadow. On a #0A0C0E ground a drop shadow
is physically invisible — there is no lighter surface for it to darken. Systems
that ship shadows into dark mode are porting a light-mode metaphor that does not
survive the transport (§5.4). Shadow appears at exactly one level: modal.
